retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note, Fact or PolicyRule rows yourself, always RETURN the row's
id alongside its text, e.g. `RETURN id(n) AS source_id, n.title AS title, n.text AS text`. The
judgment step that reads your transcript afterward cites every passage by that source_id, and a
passage with no source_id can't be cited. The skill tools already return it.

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over
writing the equivalent raw Cypher yourself in query_puppygraph — it runs a traversal that's
already known to be correct, rather than one you reconstruct from the schema notes each time.

Patient name, MRN, date of birth, and (for some review types) claim_number itself — even when
they appear inline inside a Note's or Fact's text, not just as their own property — are
de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] or [[CLAIM-0005]], not real values. The double
brackets are literal characters of the value, not markdown or wiki-link markup to strip out —
verified live: passing a "cleaned up" claim_number with the brackets removed as a tool argument
silently matches zero rows (the underlying property is the bracketed token, not the bare text
inside it), which then looks like the record has no data at all. Copy a token byte-for-byte,
brackets included, everywhere it's used: as a tool call argument, in Cypher, and quoted verbatim
in a citation. Never remark on the token format, guess what real value it stands for, or treat
its presence as unusual — a separate step restores the real values afterward, outside anything
you do here.

Once you've gathered the claim line detail, the governing policy, and at least one relevant
medical-record passage, stop calling tools and reply with a short plain-text note of what you
found. Do NOT render a Finding/No Finding determination yourself — a separate step decides
that from what you retrieve here. Don't fabricate or guess at data you haven't queried.

Audit DRG claim MR_13's full coding for this admission — this is ONE determination for the whole stay, not per code, but check every line below (not just the first) since any one of them can drive the claim-level determination.
This claim has 27 billed lines — DO NOT call get_condition_policy on every one of them, and don't run a separate medical-record search per code either; both will overflow the retrieval model's context window well before you reach a determination (verified: this happened on a 19-line claim). Triage first: look for the principal diagnosis, any CC/MCC-tier code, and any code whose severity/support looks contestable from the billed description alone, and spend your policy/note lookups on THOSE — a routine, clearly-supported comorbidity (e.g. well-documented chronic hypertension or diabetes with no CC/MCC flag) doesn't need its own policy lookup. Batch related terms into one keyword search where you can rather than one search per condition.

Billed diagnoses (position, code, description, POA/CC-MCC flags):
  1. M72.6 — Necrotizing fasciitis [POA=Y, MCC]
  2. A49.59 — Other streptococcal infection of unspecified site [POA=Y, MCC]
  3. R65.21 — Severe sepsis with septic shock [POA=Y, MCC]
  4. E11.10 — Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma [POA=Y, CC]
  5. E87.2 — Acidosis [POA=Y]

[p.845] Attending: Dr. Marcus Bell, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Admit: 2026-05-18 Transfer: 2026-09-26
LOS: 131 days
Reason for Admission: Severe DKA with concurrent necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock.
Admission Diagnoses
Severe diabetic ketoacidosis with necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolved severe DKA; resolved necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh status post surgical debridement and STSG; resolved ARDS; resolved
septic shock; contrast-induced AKI with recovery; T2DM (poor control on admission, now improving); hypertension; hyperlipidemia;
diabetic peripheral neuropathy; depression; ICU-acquired weakness.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0003]] presented with severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with septic
shock. Emergent surgical debridement was performed on admission with two additional debridements on ICU days 2 and 4. Deep tissue
cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. The course was complicated by
ARDS with successful prone positioning, contrast-induced AKI managed conservatively without RRT, mucus plugging requiring
bronchoscopy, and profound ICU-acquired weakness. Wound care with vacuum-assisted closure was ongoing throughout the stay
followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take. Diabetes management was optimized with
endocrinology consultation and the SGLT2 inhibitor was discontinued. The patient is transferred to a long-term acute care hospital for
continued wound care, rehabilitation, and diabetes management.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.2 degC | HR 79 | MAP 76 | RR 15 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: conventional nasal cannula, ambulatory. General: Alert,
interactive, comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and
rhythm; no murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft,
non-distended, +bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative;
strength improving with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance. Right thigh: skin graft in place with
excellent take; healing donor site left thigh.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 7.8 x103/uL, Hgb 10.0 g/dL, Hct 30%, platelets 220 x109/L (neutrophils 76%). BMP: Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 102, CO2 24, BUN 22,
creatinine 1.09 mg/dL, glucose 156 mg/dL, Ca 8.7, Mg 2.0, Phos 3.7. ABG (07:00): pH 7.38 / PaCO2 40 / PaO2 86 / HCO3 22; lactate
0.9 mmol/L; P/F ratio 317. Markers: procalcitonin 3.0 ng/mL, CRP 45 mg/L, troponin 0.02 ng/mL.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, and interactive. Nasal cannula 2 L. Ambulating short distances with walker; right lower extremity healing skin graft.
Tolerating diabetic diet. Hemodynamically stable. Blood glucose control improving on insulin regimen. PICC line in place for antibiotic
completion.

Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue LTAC care for wound management and rehabilitation.
2. General Surgery follow-up in 2 weeks for wound assessment.
3. Plastic Surgery follow-up in 2-4 weeks for graft evaluation.
4. Endocrinology follow-up in 2-4 weeks; hemoglobin A1c in 3 months.
5. Infectious Diseases follow-up for antibiotic course completion.
6. Primary Care follow-up for overall management.
7. Psychiatry follow-up for depression treatment.
8. Return precautions: fever, wound problems, blood glucose extremes, chest pain.

Author: Dr. Maya Rodriguez, MD (Emergency Medicine)
Date/Time: 2026-05-18 09:12
Location: Emergency Department
Chief Complaint: "I couldn't get out of bed and my leg hurts terribly."
Triage Acuity ESI 1 (resuscitation)
Arrival EMS, ground
Mode EMS, ground
Disposition Admit to Medical Intensive Care Unit
History of Present Illness (ED)
35-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes presenting with three days of severe right thigh pain, swelling, and systemic
symptoms; missed insulin doses. Found by family obtunded and tachypneic; septic shock and severe DKA identified in the field.
ED Triage / Initial Vitals
39.4 degC | HR 132 | BP 78/45 (MAP 56) | RR 32 | SpO2 92% RA; GCS 11.
Emergency Department Course & Interventions
Sepsis and DKA bundles activated. Aggressive volume resuscitation with normal saline. Insulin infusion initiated. Broad-spectrum
antimicrobials with clindamycin. Emergent CT identified necrotizing fasciitis. Surgical consultation obtained with immediate operating
room availability. Intubation for airway protection and respiratory failure. Vasopressor support with norepinephrine.
ED Medical Decision Making
Life-threatening combination of severe DKA and septic shock from necrotizing fasciitis requiring emergent surgical intervention,
aggressive metabolic resuscitation, and ICU-level care. Multi-disciplinary team activated.

[p.208] Clinician Note: Per-medication education is provided at initiation of each new medication and at discharge. Teach-back is documented
for each session. Learning barriers: critical illness and delirium early in the course; participation improved with recovery. Interpreter not
required (English).
Norepinephrine (Levophed)
Purpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.
Dose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.
Side Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.
Monitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.
Teach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.
Vancomycin
Purpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.
Dose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.
Side Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).
Monitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.
Teach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.
Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)
Purpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.
Dose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.
Side Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).
Monitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.
Teach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.
Pantoprazole (Protonix)
Purpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
Dose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.
Side Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.
Monitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.
Teach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.
Enoxaparin (Lovenox)
Purpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.
Dose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.
Side Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).
[p.172] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.
Teach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call
for help (unusual bleeding).
Insulin infusion / Sliding scale
Purpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.
Dose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.
Side Effects
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.
Monitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.
Teach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.
Amiodarone
Purpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).
Dose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.
Side Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use
sunscreen.
Monitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.
Teach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials
provided.
Apixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge
Purpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).
Dose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.
Side Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.
Monitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.

        - **Distinctions Required**: Should distinguish from other codes such as cellulitis (L03.90) and myositis (M60.009), which require confirming fascial involvement. 
        - **Validation Criteria**: Documentation must include operative finding of necrotizing fasciitis such as gross evidence, imaging, or specific clinical pathways.

2. **R65.21 - Severe sepsis with septic shock [POA=Y, MCC]**
    - **Governing Condition Policy Findings:**

3. **J80 - Acute respiratory distress syndrome [POA=N, MCC]**

- **Procedure Notes**: Document the urgent surgical interventions performed with specific tissue removal amounts noted firmly establishing continued improvement.

### Discharge Disposition
- The documented discharge status states the patient was transferred to a long-term acute care hospital for ongoing wound care, rehabilitation, and management of diabetes.

### Conclusion

However, any nuances around care transitions or ongoing interventions can refine future audit focus, especially where the medical record is inconsistent or suggests a conflict regarding documentation vitality (e.g., the involvement of overlapping comorbidities). judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;

Procedures billed include emergent debridement codes and a full-thickness autologous skin replacement code 0HRJX73 (full thickness) and platelet transfusion 30280B1.\n\nKey determinations and reasoning with evidence:\n1) Principal diagnosis sequencing error — position 1 should be E11.10 (DKA), not M72.6 (necrotizing fasciitis).\n   - The facility's own inpatient problem/principal-diagnosis header lists DKA first: Principal Diagnosis DKA; necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh; septic shock (INPATIENT MEDICAL RECORD, p.1) (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1). Ev: ev5\n   - The admitting H&P and assessment document severe diabetic ketoacidosis as the presenting problem complicated by necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock: Assessment — 35-year-old ... severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis ... septic shock (History & Physical, p.541). Ev: ev4\n   Therefore the documentation shows DKA occasioned admission and should be sequenced as principal (E11.10). Keeping M72.6 as a secondary diagnosis is appropriate given the operative and imaging confirmation below.\n\n2) Necrotizing fasciitis (M72.6) is supported clinically (but should be secondary, not principal).\n   - CT right thigh: Impression: Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes (Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Right Thigh with IV Contrast, p.421). Ev: ev1\n   - Operative report: Extensive necrosis of skin, subcutaneous tissue, and superficial fascia identified; debridement performed to viable tissue with removal of necrotic tissue (Procedure Note - Emergent Surgical Debridement - Right Thigh, p.41). Ev: ev2\n   These satisfy the policy validation criteria (operative confirmation) for M72.6 (MCC) but do not change the sequencing decision above. \n\n3) Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21, MCC) is supported and appropriately coded as an MCC, present on admission (POA=Y).\n   - ED and admitting documentation record septic shock on presentation and vasopressor use: \"Found by family obtunded and tachypneic; septic shock and severe DKA identified in the field\" (Emergency Department Provider Note, p.541) and the H&P explicitly describes septic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n8; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9). Ev: ev3, ev4\n   - Early ICU flowsheets/ABG and lactate are consistent with shock (Critical Care Progress Note shows lactate 4.9 and P/F 63). Ev: ev10\n   The R65.21 assignment (MCC) is supported by provider documentation of septic shock and objective data (vasopressor use and elevated lactate). Note: the facility did not sequence an A40/A41 organism-specific sepsis code as principal; the record does identify organisms (see ID consult) — this sequencing/organism-specific-code choice is discussed below but does not negate R65.21 support.\n\n4) Acute respiratory distress syndrome (J80) — POA flag incorrect on the claim (billed POA=N). Admission H&P documents ARDS as an active problem on admission and early ABG/ventilator data meet ARDS oxygenation thresholds.\n   - Admission problem list includes: \"6 | Acute respiratory failure with ARDS - resolved\" in the admitting H&P (History & Physical, p.541), i.e., provider documentation at admission supports ARDS present on admission. Ev: ev6\n   - Early ABG/ventilator data show severe hypoxemia / P/F ratio 63 (Critical Care Progress Note, 05-18, ABG 02:00 with PaO2 60; P/F 63) supporting ARDS physiology (Critical Care Progress Note, p.84). Ev: ev10\n   - Radiology / consult notes document ARDS during the encounter (Nephrology note: Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Bilateral opacities compatible with ARDS). Ev: ev11\n   Conclusion: the record contains provider documentation of ARDS at/near admission plus objective oxygenation data; J80 should be POA=Y rather than POA=N.\n\n5) Unsupported / incorrectly coded diagnoses removed:\n   - E11.22 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease) — remove: nephrology and discharge documentation describe contrast-induced AKI with recovery and do not document chronic diabetic CKD. \"AKI multifactorial from DKA, sepsis, and iodinated contrast exposure. Creatinine peak 2.4; urine output maintained with resuscitation\" (Nephrology Consultation, p.779). Ev: ev7; Discharge notes list \"contrast-induced AKI with recovery\" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.845). Ev: ev8\n   - G93.6 (Cerebral edema) — remove: there is no provider documentation of cerebral edema; serial progress notes document neurologic recovery (Neuro at transfer: A&Ox3, CAM-ICU negative, strength improving) inconsistent with a diagnosis of cerebral edema (Critical Care Progress Note, 06-11, p.494). Ev: ev12\n   Rationale: Neither the consulting notes nor discharge summary document cerebral edema as a diagnosed complication; the record instead documents recovery of mental status.\n\n6) Unsupported / miscoded procedures removed:\n   - 0HRJX73 (Replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness) — remove: the chart documents a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous tissue substitute. Nursing progress note documents: \"Split-thickness skin graft placement; foam bolster in place.\" (Nursing Progress Note - Day Shift, p.345). Ev: ev9; Discharge summary describes \"split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18\" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.845). Ev: ev8\n   - 30280B1 (Transfusion of nonautologous platelets into central vein, open approach) — remove: the record documents post-operative anemia requiring transfusion but provides no explicit documentation of platelet transfusion; the problem list states \"Post-operative anemia requiring transfusion\" (History & Physical - Active Problem List, p.541) without specifying platelets (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9). Ev: ev13\n   Rationale: The nursing and discharge documentation specifically describe an STSG (split-thickness) rather than a full-thickness autologous-skin replacement PCS code; billed full-thickness code (0HRJX73) is therefore unsupported. For the platelet transfusion PCS (30280B1), the record documents a transfusion for anemia but does not document platelet transfusion — insufficient support for this specific PCS.\n\n7) Ventilator status code (Z99.11) removed: discharge documentation documents the patient on low-flow nasal cannula and tolerating trach collar at transfer (Discharge/Transfer Summary: \"Airway/Support: conventional nasal cannula, ambulatory\" and transfer instructions to LTAC), i.e., dependence on respirator does not persist at discharge and is therefore not appropriate to remain coded. Ev: ev8\n\nBottom line corrective actions (claim-level):\n- Sequence change: make E11.10 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis) principal (position 1) per the admitting documentation (H&P and facility principal-diagnosis header). Ev: ev5, ev4\n- Keep M72.6 (necrotizing fasciitis) as secondary (supported by CT and operative notes). Ev: ev1, ev2\n- Keep R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock, MCC) (supported by ED/H&P documentation of septic shock and vasopressor use). Ev: ev3, ev4\n- Change J80 POA indicator from N to Y (supported by admitting H&P and early ABG/P/F). Ev: ev6, ev10\n- Remove E11.22 (diabetic CKD) and G93.6 (cerebral edema) for lack of supporting documentation. Ev: ev7, ev8, ev12\n- Remove 0HRJX73 (full-thickness autologous skin replacement) and 30280B1 (platelet transfusion) as the chart documents split-thickness skin graft and an unspecified transfusion for anemia rather than platelet transfusion. Ev: ev9, ev8, ev13\n\nAll citations above are to: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf sections and pages as indicated next to each evidence id (ev1..ev13).",
  "rationale_letter": "To: Medical Records/Coding Department\nRe: MR_13 — DRG coding determination and required corrections\n\nDear Provider/Coder,\n\nAn audit of the inpatient stay MR_13 (admit 05/18/2026) was performed comparing billed diagnoses/procedures to the medical record and governing DRG coding policy. Based on the chart documentation and applicable policy, the audit identified the following Findings requiring correction:\n\n1) Principal diagnosis sequencing error (Finding): The admitting documentation and facility problem list identify severe diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) as the condition that occasioned admission. Specifically, the inpatient header lists \"Principal Diagnosis DKA; necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh; septic shock\" and the admitting H&P documents \"severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis ... with septic shock\" (History & Physical, 05/18/2026; Inpatient Record header). Therefore E11.10 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis) should be the principal diagnosis (position 1) on the claim rather than M72.6. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1 (Inpatient record header) and NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9 (H&P, 05/18/2026).\n\n2) Necrotizing fasciitis (M72.6) is supported but should be coded as a secondary diagnosis: CT imaging documents gas in the fascial planes and the operative debridement note documents gross fascial necrosis and debridement to viable tissue (CT Right Thigh, 05/18/2026; Procedure Note - Emergent Surgical Debridement, 05/18/2026). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n13; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n16.\n\n3) Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21, MCC) is supported and appropriately carries MCC: the ED and admitting notes state septic shock on presentation and document vasopressor support and elevated lactate. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n8; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9.\n\n4) ARDS POA indicator is incorrect: Admission documentation includes \"Acute respiratory failure with ARDS\" on the admitting problem list, and early ABG/ventilator data meet ARDS oxygenation thresholds (P/F 63). J80 should be POA=Y. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n11; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n43.\n\n5) Unsupported diagnoses removed:\n   - E11.22 (T2DM with diabetic chronic kidney disease): nephrology consultation documents AKI due to DKA/sepsis/contrast with recovery; the record does not support chronic diabetic CKD. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n43; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1118.\n   - G93.6 (Cerebral edema): no provider documentation of cerebral edema was found; serial notes document neurologic recovery (A&Ox3, CAM-ICU negative) inconsistent with a diagnosis of cerebral edema. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n165; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1118.\n\n6) Unsupported/incorrect procedure codes removed:\n   - 0HRJX73 (full-thickness autologous skin replacement): the record documents split-thickness skin graft placement (nursing note and discharge summary). The billed full-thickness autologous tissue substitute PCS is not supported. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n125; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1118.\n   - 30280B1 (platelet transfusion): the problem list documents post-operative anemia requiring transfusion but the record contains no documentation of platelet transfusion specifically; insufficient evidence to support this procedure code. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9.\n\nCorrection being made to the claim (summary):\n- Principal diagnosis changed to E11.10 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis) (position 1).\n- M72.6 retained as secondary (supported by CT and operative findings).\n- J80 POA flag changed to Y.\n- Remove E11.22 and G93.6 for lack of documentation.\n- Remove PCS 0HRJX73 and 30280B1 due to lack of specific supporting documentation for those exact PCS descriptors.\n\nIf you disagree with these corrections, please provide targeted clinical documentation within 30 days that supports: (a) why necrotizing fasciitis, rather than DKA, occasioned the admission (if you believe M72.6 should remain principal), (b) documentation of cerebral edema (if G93.6 is to be retained), (c) documentation of chronic diabetic CKD (if E11.22 is to be retained), (d) operative/procedure documentation explicitly supporting full-thickness autologous skin replacement (0HRJX73) or platelet transfusion (30280B1). Absent contemporaneous provider documentation meeting the cited validation criteria, the above corrections will stand.\n\nSincerely,\nClinical Audit Team\n",

result.finding_category: Principal diagnosis sequencing error; incorrect POA & unsupported codes/procedures
result.system_note: Summary of audit and cited evidence (document / section / page): - What was billed: Principal diagnosis M72.6 (Necrotizing fasciitis) is billed in position 1; the claim also lists R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock), J80 (ARDS POA=N), Z99.11 (dependence on respirator POA=N), G93.6 (cerebral edema POA=N), and E11.22 (T2DM with CKD) among other diagnoses. Procedures billed include emergent debridement codes and a full-thickness autologous skin replacement code 0HRJX73 (full thickness) and platelet transfusion 30280B1. Key determinations and reasoning with evidence: 1) Principal diagnosis sequencing error - position 1 should be E11.10 (DKA), not M72.6 (necrotizing fasciitis). - The facility's own inpatient problem/principal-diagnosis header lists DKA first: Principal Diagnosis DKA; necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh; septic shock (INPATIENT MEDICAL RECORD, p.1) (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1). Ev: ev5 - The admitting H&P and assessment document severe diabetic ketoacidosis as the presenting problem complicated by necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock: Assessment - 35-year-old ... severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis ... septic shock (History & Physical, p.541). Ev: ev4 Therefore the documentation shows DKA occasioned admission and should be sequenced as principal (E11.10). Keeping M72.6 as a secondary diagnosis is appropriate given the operative and imaging confirmation below. 2) Necrotizing fasciitis (M72.6) is supported clinically (but should be secondary, not principal). - CT right thigh: Impression: Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes (Diagnostic Imaging Report - CT Right Thigh with IV Contrast, p.421). Ev: ev1 - Operative report: Extensive necrosis of skin, subcutaneous tissue, and superficial fascia identified; debridement performed to viable tissue with removal of necrotic tissue (Procedure Note - Emergent Surgical Debridement - Right Thigh, p.41). Ev: ev2 These satisfy the policy validation criteria (operative confirmation) for M72.6 (MCC) but do not change the sequencing decision above. 3) Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21, MCC) is supported and appropriately coded as an MCC, present on admission (POA=Y). - ED and admitting documentation record septic shock on presentation and vasopressor use: "Found by family obtunded and tachypneic; septic shock and severe DKA identified in the field" (Emergency Department Provider Note, p.541) and the H&P explicitly describes septic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n8; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9). Ev: ev3, ev4 - Early ICU flowsheets/ABG and lactate are consistent with shock (Critical Care Progress Note shows lactate 4.9 and P/F 63). Ev: ev10 The R65.21 assignment (MCC) is supported by provider documentation of septic shock and objective data (vasopressor use and elevated lactate). Note: the facility did not sequence an A40/A41 organism-specific sepsis code as principal; the record does identify organisms (see ID consult) - this sequencing/organism-specific-code choice is discussed below but does not negate R65.21 support. 4) Acute respiratory distress syndrome (J80) - POA flag incorrect on the claim (billed POA=N). Admission H&P documents ARDS as an active problem on admission and early ABG/ventilator data meet ARDS oxygenation thresholds. - Admission problem list includes: "6 | Acute respiratory failure with ARDS - resolved" in the admitting H&P (History & Physical, p.541), i.e., provider documentation at admission supports ARDS present on admission. Ev: ev6 - Early ABG/ventilator data show severe hypoxemia / P/F ratio 63 (Critical Care Progress Note, 05-18, ABG 02:00 with PaO2 60; P/F 63) supporting ARDS physiology (Critical Care Progress Note, p.84). Ev: ev10 - Radiology / consult notes document ARDS during the encounter (Nephrology note: Chest Radiograph, Portable AP: Bilateral opacities compatible with ARDS). Ev: ev11 Conclusion: the record contains provider documentation of ARDS at/near admission plus objective oxygenation data; J80 should be POA=Y rather than POA=N. 5) Unsupported / incorrectly coded diagnoses removed: - E11.22 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease) - remove: nephrology and discharge documentation describe contrast-induced AKI with recovery and do not document chronic diabetic CKD. "AKI multifactorial from DKA, sepsis, and iodinated contrast exposure. Creatinine peak 2.4; urine output maintained with resuscitation" (Nephrology Consultation, p.779). Ev: ev7; Discharge notes list "contrast-induced AKI with recovery" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.845). Ev: ev8 - G93.6 (Cerebral edema) - remove: there is no provider documentation of cerebral edema; serial progress notes document neurologic recovery (Neuro at transfer: A&Ox3, CAM-ICU negative, strength improving) inconsistent with a diagnosis of cerebral edema (Critical Care Progress Note, 06-11, p.494). Ev: ev12 Rationale: Neither the consulting notes nor discharge summary document cerebral edema as a diagnosed complication; the record instead documents recovery of mental status. 6) Unsupported / miscoded procedures removed: - 0HRJX73 (Replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness) - remove: the chart documents a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous tissue substitute. Nursing progress note documents: "Split-thickness skin graft placement; foam bolster in place." (Nursing Progress Note - Day Shift, p.345). Ev: ev9; Discharge summary describes "split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18" (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.845). Ev: ev8 - 30280B1 (Transfusion of nonautologous platelets into central vein, open approach) - remove: the record documents post-operative anemia requiring transfusion but provides no explicit documentation of platelet transfusion; the problem list states "Post-operative anemia requiring transfusion" (History & Physical - Active Problem List, p.541) without specifying platelets (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9). Ev: ev13 Rationale: The nursing and discharge documentation specifically describe an STSG (split-thickness) rather than a full-thickness autologous-skin replacement PCS code; billed full-thickness code (0HRJX73) is therefore unsupported. For the platelet transfusion PCS (30280B1), the record documents a transfusion for anemia but does not document platelet transfusion - insufficient support for this specific PCS. 7) Ventilator status code (Z99.11) removed: discharge documentation documents the patient on low-flow nasal cannula and tolerating trach collar at transfer (Discharge/Transfer Summary: "Airway/Support: conventional nasal cannula, ambulatory" and transfer instructions to LTAC), i.e., dependence on respirator does not persist at discharge and is therefore not appropriate to remain coded. Ev: ev8 Bottom line corrective actions (claim-level): - Sequence change: make E11.10 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis) principal (position 1) per the admitting documentation (H&P and facility principal-diagnosis header). Ev: ev5, ev4 - Keep M72.6 (necrotizing fasciitis) as secondary (supported by CT and operative notes). Ev: ev1, ev2 - Keep R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock, MCC) (supported by ED/H&P documentation of septic shock and vasopressor use). Ev: ev3, ev4 - Change J80 POA indicator from N to Y (supported by admitting H&P and early ABG/P/F). Ev: ev6, ev10 - Remove E11.22 (diabetic CKD) and G93.6 (cerebral edema) for lack of supporting documentation. Ev: ev7, ev8, ev12 - Remove 0HRJX73 (full-thickness autologous skin replacement) and 30280B1 (platelet transfusion) as the chart documents split-thickness skin graft and an unspecified transfusion for anemia rather than platelet transfusion. Ev: ev9, ev8, ev13 All citations above are to: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf sections and pages as indicated next to each evidence id (ev1..ev13).
result.rationale_letter: To: Medical Records/Coding Department Re: MR_13 - DRG coding determination and required corrections Dear Provider/Coder, An audit of the inpatient stay MR_13 (admit 05/18/2026) was performed comparing billed diagnoses/procedures to the medical record and governing DRG coding policy. Based on the chart documentation and applicable policy, the audit identified the following Findings requiring correction: 1) Principal diagnosis sequencing error (Finding): The admitting documentation and facility problem list identify severe diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) as the condition that occasioned admission. Specifically, the inpatient header lists "Principal Diagnosis DKA; necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh; septic shock" and the admitting H&P documents "severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis ... with septic shock" (History & Physical, 05/18/2026; Inpatient Record header). Therefore E11.10 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis) should be the principal diagnosis (position 1) on the claim rather than M72.6. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1 (Inpatient record header) and NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9 (H&P, 05/18/2026). 2) Necrotizing fasciitis (M72.6) is supported but should be coded as a secondary diagnosis: CT imaging documents gas in the fascial planes and the operative debridement note documents gross fascial necrosis and debridement to viable tissue (CT Right Thigh, 05/18/2026; Procedure Note - Emergent Surgical Debridement, 05/18/2026). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n13; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n16. 3) Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21, MCC) is supported and appropriately carries MCC: the ED and admitting notes state septic shock on presentation and document vasopressor support and elevated lactate. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n8; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9. 4) ARDS POA indicator is incorrect: Admission documentation includes "Acute respiratory failure with ARDS" on the admitting problem list, and early ABG/ventilator data meet ARDS oxygenation thresholds (P/F 63). J80 should be POA=Y. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n11; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n43. 5) Unsupported diagnoses removed: - E11.22 (T2DM with diabetic chronic kidney disease): nephrology consultation documents AKI due to DKA/sepsis/contrast with recovery; the record does not support chronic diabetic CKD. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n43; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1118. - G93.6 (Cerebral edema): no provider documentation of cerebral edema was found; serial notes document neurologic recovery (A&Ox3, CAM-ICU negative) inconsistent with a diagnosis of cerebral edema. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n165; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1118. 6) Unsupported/incorrect procedure codes removed: - 0HRJX73 (full-thickness autologous skin replacement): the record documents split-thickness skin graft placement (nursing note and discharge summary). The billed full-thickness autologous tissue substitute PCS is not supported. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n125; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n1118. - 30280B1 (platelet transfusion): the problem list documents post-operative anemia requiring transfusion but the record contains no documentation of platelet transfusion specifically; insufficient evidence to support this procedure code. Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_13.pdf-n9. Correction being made to the claim (summary): - Principal diagnosis changed to E11.10 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis) (position 1). - M72.6 retained as secondary (supported by CT and operative findings). - J80 POA flag changed to Y. - Remove E11.22 and G93.6 for lack of documentation. - Remove PCS 0HRJX73 and 30280B1 due to lack of specific supporting documentation for those exact PCS descriptors. If you disagree with these corrections, please provide targeted clinical documentation within 30 days that supports: (a) why necrotizing fasciitis, rather than DKA, occasioned the admission (if you believe M72.6 should remain principal), (b) documentation of cerebral edema (if G93.6 is to be retained), (c) documentation of chronic diabetic CKD (if E11.22 is to be retained), (d) operative/procedure documentation explicitly supporting full-thickness autologous skin replacement (0HRJX73) or platelet transfusion (30280B1). Absent contemporaneous provider documentation meeting the cited validation criteria, the above corrections will stand. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team

citation_checks.quote: Assessment 35-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (last A1c 12.4%), hypertension, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy who presented with three days of severe right thigh pain and swelling, nausea, vomiting, and progressive weakness. Family notes that the patient had been missing insulin doses for the past week due to depression and was using an SGLT2 inhibitor. On EMS arrival at home, the patient was found obtunded with tachypnea and hypotension. Right thigh was noted to be swollen, erythematous, and tender with palpable crepitus. Field glucose was 542 mg/dL and ketones were positive. IV fluid resuscitation was initiated en route. In the ED, the patient was in severe DKA (pH 6.98, bicarbonate 5) and septic shock. CT scan confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained. Broad-spectrum antibiotics including clindamycin for toxin suppression were initiated.
Principal Diagnosis DKA; necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh; septic shock
